_note: Static country-level markers for networks with no physical station pins. Consumed by index.html alongside stations.json. THIS FILE IS USER-FACING: every `note` and `yearly_cost` string renders directly in map popup tooltips for hobbyists. See `_note_field_convention` and `_yearly_cost_convention` below before editing.
_rules_doc: Process and editing rules: country_markers.proc.md (same dir). Pipeline context (how this file relates to docs/networks.md and docs/country-survey.md): ../docs/pipeline.md.
_note_field_convention: The popup auto-renders the access label, yearly_cost, region, note, and registration URL — so `note` should ADD information beyond those, not restate them. DO NOT: repeat the price (it's in yearly_cost), repeat the access label ('Paid subscription required' is already shown), restate the region, include the registration URL inline (it renders separately), or instruct the user to 'contact X' (link to the website via `registration` instead). DO include, when applicable: station count once ('78 stations'), free hobbyist alternatives ('Volunteer rtk2go/Centipede bases provide partial free coverage'), terminal access blockers in plain words, real safety/operational warnings, non-obvious access mechanics. Tone: matter-of-fact, hobbyist-addressed, ≤2 short sentences typical, ~250 chars max. Skip the field entirely if there's nothing useful to add.
_yearly_cost_convention: Single short line, one of: '$X/yr' (USD), '€X/yr (~$Y/yr)' / '£X/yr' / '¥X/yr' / '₹X/yr' / '₽X/yr' / 'S$X/yr' (symbol currencies), or 'X CCY/yr (~$Y/yr)' for ISO-only codes (CHF, SEK, NOK, RSD, etc.). Drop the '~' prefix unless the figure is genuinely uncertain (estimates are implicit). If pricing is not published, OMIT the field entirely so the line disappears from the popup — do not write 'pricing not publicly listed' there. Multi-tier pricing: lead with the primary tier; mention any hobbyist-relevant secondary tier in `note`. Local-currency qualifiers (e.g. 'private users only') belong in `note`, not `yearly_cost`.
_tiers: Five values describing the network's nature from a hobbyist's perspective: 'free' (no fee to use; coloured circle if in-pipeline + has data, grey circle otherwise; note must truthfully open with 'N stations, free.' when no data is ingested yet); 'paid' (commercial subscription, hobbyist can buy access; circled-? marker; yearly_cost recommended); 'paid-affordable' (paid but under ~$200/yr or otherwise hobbyist-reachable; circled-? marker); 'restricted' (no hobbyist path at any price — vetted partners, sector-only, no published rate; circled-? marker); 'weird' (something interesting to a target user that doesn't fit the other tiers — non-standard NTRIP, active jamming/spoofing, infrastructure too sparse to work, war-disrupted, free RINEX-only PPK alternative without real-time NTRIP, network announced/under construction but not yet operational, government CORS distributed only via licensed commercial resellers, micro-state with no local service; circled-? marker, note carries the explanation). The tier drives marker style; whether station data exists is derived at runtime from stations.json (in-pipeline + data → coloured pins/circle; otherwise → grey circle for free, circled-? for the others).
_vrs_flag: Optional 'vrs': true means the network delivers VRS / network-RTK streams (a virtual reference station near the rover) rather than a single physical antenna. Orthogonal to tier — a network can be free+vrs (KSA-CORS, SAPOS), paid+vrs (swipos, HEPOS), restricted+vrs (DVRS, KazGeoDesy), etc. Absence of the flag means nothing — either the network is single-base, or VRS-status is unknown / not relevant. The flag is informational; the renderer uses it together with data presence to decide visuals (free+vrs+ingested → coloured ring; free+vrs+not-ingested → grey ring; non-VRS free entries with pins fall through to physical pins from stations.json).

markers.name: ASG-EUPOS
markers.note: Free since 2 Oct 2022. Registration approval 1–2 working days.

markers.name: CROPOS
markers.note: RTK (VPPS) is free since Apr 2022. A one-time 40 EUR registration fee applies per Regulation NN 56/2023.

markers.name: ESTPOS
markers.note: Free under a 2025 directive through 31 Aug 2026; tariff after that date not announced. Portal account and service agreement required.

markers.name: ReNEP
markers.note: Mainland + Azores + Madeira. New Funchal station added May 2026.

markers.name: ZAKPOS
markers.note: Nationwide network, hub at Mukachevo (western Ukraine). Wartime-reduced rate (April 2025). Pauses automatically during air-raid alerts.

markers.name: UA-System.NET
markers.note: Largest commercial network in Ukraine; 200+ stations, Leica VRS platform. Shorter terms available. Wartime discount plans for eastern and southern oblasts.

markers.name: RTK HUB
markers.note: Nationwide commercial RTK network (formerly TNT-TPI). Caster address disclosed after registration. Wartime-reduced rate.

markers.name: Kyivstar mAgri.RTK
markers.note: 97 stations, Trimble VRS + Nearest; requires Kyivstar contract. xFill Premium continuity. Pauses during air-raid alerts.

markers.name: GPSBru / AGN
markers.note: Single station (UKKE) at Uccle observatory; host:port issued after AGN login request. Useful within ~20 km of Brussels.

markers.name: UGRF CORS
markers.note: Single-base, VRS, MAC (incl. iMAX) and FKP mountpoints.

markers.name: ETCORS
markers.note: 10-station national network launched Dec 2024 by SSGI; planned expansion to ~200. No public NTRIP endpoint or access terms published — contact SSGI directly.

markers.name: Muya CORS
markers.note: Pay-as-you-go vouchers via M-Pesa; longer hourly/daily/monthly tiers offered at checkout but not itemised publicly. Practical to pay only from a Kenyan mobile wallet.

markers.name: BF-CORS
markers.note: 13 CORS stations (established 2011–2018) managed by IGB; post-processing RINEX is the documented service. No confirmed public NTRIP RTK caster. Ongoing armed conflict covers ~40–60% of the country.

markers.name: KyrPOS
markers.note: Signup is a 9-step paper-contract flow (download, mail, sign, bank transfer) — practical only with a Kyrgyz postal address and bank account. Minimum 1-month subscription. Caster port appears geo-filtered.

markers.name: Khmer GEONET
markers.note: JICA-built pilot CORS at 5 sites (Phnom Penh, Kandal, Kampong Speu, Siem Reap, Stung Treng); free trial period in force through 1 Jul 2026. Registration runs through a Trimble Pivot web admin; standard NTRIP host:port not publicly advertised. ~200 km gaps between stations.

markers.name: Myanmar Survey Department CORS
markers.note: Built 2019 by the Survey Department (3 to IGS standard) for internal geodetic use. No public NTRIP endpoint, mountpoint list, or registration channel; post-2021-coup operational status unverified. Nearest free RTK base is in Bangladesh (~430 km), far beyond useful single-base range.

markers.name: PACI / Kuwait Municipality CORS
markers.note: 14-station government CORS network jointly operated by PACI and Kuwait Municipality; streams issued only to licensed surveying firms under municipal contract. No individual or hobbyist path at any price. No public NTRIP host:port published.

markers.name: Lands & Survey CORS
markers.note: 4-station government CORS (CIGD11 datum). An RTK subscription exists but the host:port, mountpoints, and RTK price are not on the public page — access runs through the Chief Surveyor's office. The caymanlandinfo.ky tier prices (Bronze 3 300 / Silver 4 950 / Gold 7 150 / Platinum 12 100 KYD per year) are mapping-only and do NOT include RTK.

markers.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
markers.note: No national NTRIP service. UWI Seismic Research Centre runs scientific cGPS (STKN on St. Kitts, BATH on Nevis) since 2007 but does not stream RTK. Nearest free real-time base is EarthScope NOTA RDON on Redonda (~35 km south of Nevis, NULA non-commercial).

markers.name: DOL LandGNSS
markers.note: Free trial, but registration requires a Thai national ID — foreign visitors cannot self-register. Volunteer rtk2go bases inside Thailand offer a foreign-accessible fallback.

markers.name: TPOS
markers.note: 11 stations, free. Self-service portal; no professional licence required. RTK, VRS/MAX/NRT mountpoints, and 1-year historical data archive.

markers.name: STPOS
markers.note: 10 stations, free. Online registration; ID + intended-use declaration required to activate RTK (RINEX available immediately). No professional restriction.

markers.name: Rete GNSS Veneto
markers.note: ~20 stations, free. Open to any user; credentials assigned by email after registration. Multiple stream formats available.

markers.name: Rete GNSS Liguria
markers.note: 10 stations, free. 7 Liguria stations + 3 shared with SPIN3 GNSS (northern border).

markers.name: Sicili@net
markers.note: ~80 stations (INGV Catania seismic network), free. Credentials assigned by email after registration. Multiple stream formats including VRS (virtual reference station).

markers.name: SARNET
markers.note: Commercial network (SARNET s.r.l.). RTK, VRS, DGPS, and RINEX archive. Sardinia-specific network; HxGN SmartNet Italy (ItalPOS) also covers Sardinia as part of its national service. Operational status uncertain — see block note.

markers.name: HxGN SmartNet Italy (ItalPOS)
markers.note: Nationwide commercial VRS network (ItalPOS). Useful where no free regional caster exists, e.g. Sardinia and central/northern Calabria (southern Calabria is covered free by sicilianet). Professional focus; no explicit hobbyist ban.

markers.name: ACORN
markers.note: Alaska DNR / DOTPF / NPS / EarthScope partnership. Four regional VRS solutions (South Central, Interior, Southeast, Northwest) plus a Norton Sound experimental VRS and a nearest-station single-base stream.

markers.name: NPS CORS
markers.note: Single-base mountpoints across CONUS, Alaska, Hawaii, American Samoa, and the Marianas. Operated by the National Park Service; credentials are provisioned manually and whether access extends beyond NPS partners is unclear.

markers.name: REMOS
markers.note: ~8 stations active per IGVSB website; intended free but no public endpoint confirmed. Commercial alternative: acnovo.net (~USD 20/period). GPS jamming around Venezuelan airspace was reported Sep–Dec 2025 (FAA advisory MAIQUETIA FIR, Nov 2025–Feb 2026).

markers.name: RED-GEO CORS NTRIP
markers.note: ~7 base stations nationwide (La Paz, Cochabamba, Oruro, Sacaba, Tarija, Santa Cruz, Yacuiba). Access requires phone registration — no self-service portal or published pricing.

markers.name: HEPOS
markers.note: 98 stations, full GNSS. €160/quarter (~$170) for seasonal use. Pay-per-minute bundle (€90+VAT) for occasional access. Individual sign-up online, no professional licence required.

markers.name: URANUS / TopNET Live Greece
markers.note: 117 stations covering Greece and Cyprus. 3-day free trial available. HEPOS (€480/yr) is a public-sector alternative with confirmed pricing.

markers.name: ROMPOS
markers.note: VAT included. Monthly subscription also available (100 RON/mo). Pricing set by ANCPI Order 16/2019.

markers.name: Orphéon
markers.note: ~215–220 stations. Commercial VRS network; individual subscriptions available. Centipede RTK (crtk.net:2101) provides free nationwide coverage as a Volunteer alternative.

markers.name: Teria
markers.note: ~187 stations. Operated by Exagone SAS for Ordre des Géomètres-Experts. Centipede RTK (crtk.net:2101) provides free nationwide coverage.

markers.name: swipos
markers.note: At this price a local base station is likely more practical. Volunteer rtk2go/Centipede bases provide partial free coverage on the Swiss plateau.

markers.name: CPOS / ETPOS
markers.note: Agriculture tier NOK 5,000/yr; standard surveying tier NOK 11,000/yr (both ex-VAT). 1-month free trial for new customers. Volunteer rtk2go/Centipede bases cover populated areas south of ~63°N.

markers.name: SIGNAL
markers.note: Early-discount tier sometimes available — confirm with GURS before paying. Volunteer rtk2go/Centipede bases provide partial free coverage.

markers.name: SWEPOS Network RTK
markers.note: 10-day free trial for new customers. The included DGNSS sub-service is sub-metre only, not centimetre RTK. Shorter-commitment blocks (90 days, 1,000-minute pot) also available.

markers.name: SiReNT
markers.note: 3-day trial available but requires SingPass (Singapore residents only).

markers.name: MyRTKnet
markers.note: JUPEM operates this as a cost-recovery service mandated by the Survey Act; no free national alternative. One rtk2go volunteer base near Malacca is the only no-cost option.

markers.name: TUSAGA-Aktif
markers.note: Online registration requires a Turkish national ID (TC Kimlik No) — foreign users cannot self-register. Monthly (₺1,000) and 6-month (₺6,000) plans available for occasional use. ₺550 one-time device registration fee also applies. Prices include VAT.

markers.name: VNGEONET
markers.note: Foreigners can register with a passport. Monthly (750,000 VNĐ) and 6-month (4,280,000 VNĐ) plans also available. A free annual tier exists in zones with >80 km station spacing — relevant outside the densely covered river deltas.

markers.name: PAGeNet
markers.note: No annual plan; the per-hour tier (PHP 100/hr, ~$1.77/hr) is the only one within the hobbyist cutoff. Day (~$18) and 15-day (~$133) tiers exist. PHP 1,000 (~$18) one-time registration. Non-Metro Manila clients pay by LandBank deposit — a practical barrier for foreigners.

markers.name: GNSSnet.hu
markers.note: A 30-day local-radius pass (~€38, within 50 km of one point) or pay-per-minute billing (~€1.20–1.80/hr) suits a short project. One-time €30 registration fee.

markers.name: AGROS
markers.note: Trimble VRS Now backbone. Hourly and monthly packages also available. Serbian-language portal only.

markers.name: GeoNet GEO-RTK
markers.note: The only commercial caster identified in Bulgaria (gnss.geonet.bg:2101), distributed by Solitech AD. Cheapest occasional-use tier is ГеоНет 150 at €15/mo with 150 RTK minutes included (24-month contract). 6 rtk2go and 2 Centipede volunteer bases provide partial free single-base coverage of central, northern and eastern Bulgaria.

markers.name: MONTEPOS
markers.note: 9 CORS stations. Subscription plans from 24 hours to 2 years. Host:port issued after account creation.

markers.name: SRPOS
markers.note: Republika Srpska half of the BiHPOS network. ~17 stations, VRS + FKP + iMAX. Shorter prepaid blocks: 10 hours (~$17), 20 hours (~$29), 1 month (~$145). KM is pegged to the euro at 1.95583.

markers.name: FBiHPOS
markers.note: Federation of BiH half of the BiHPOS network. ~17 stations, VRS + MAX + iMAX. Caster at fbihpos.katastar.ba port 8080 (not the standard 2101). Shorter plans: 7 days (~$87), 1 month (~$145). 100 KM (~$58) one-time registration fee. Open to private individuals.

markers.name: e-GNSS
markers.note: Pay-per-use; 78 stations, VBS-RTK. Caster and portal both appear geo-blocked from outside Taiwan, so foreign users face a non-trivial registration path. Annual contracts available for regular users.

markers.name: CZEPOS
markers.note: Free only for education and government bodies. Hourly tariff also available (50 CZK/hr RTK/VRS, 60 CZK/hr DGPS) under vyhláška 31/1995 Sb.

markers.name: SKPOS
markers.note: ~26 stations. Monthly plans suit short projects. Registration accepts private individuals from most countries — no trade licence required. Free for Slovak public-sector bodies.

markers.name: SoI CORS
markers.note: Free only for central/state government and academic users. Paid private subscription requires Aadhaar or PAN ID — effectively Indian residents only.

markers.name: Tamil Nadu State CORS
markers.note: Closed cadastral infrastructure used by the Tamil Nadu Department of Survey and Settlement. No public NTRIP service or tariff. Not currently part of SoI CORS.

markers.name: Réseau GNSS du Québec (MRNF)
markers.note: 18 free government reference stations (MRNF — formerly MERN/MRN), but NOT standard NTRIP — each station delivers a raw TCP stream (per-station IP:port, CMR+/RTCM 3.2). Standard NTRIP clients will not connect; you need a TCP-capable receiver (e.g. Emlid RS2) or an RTKLIB str2str bridge.

markers.name: BC RTN
markers.note: Subscription portal currently unavailable (government website reorganisation); check the registration link for updates. No Canadian province offers free public NTRIP.

markers.name: Nova Scotia NSACS
markers.note: 40 government reference stations; real-time corrections only via paid commercial resellers (HxGN SmartNet, Can-Net, Brandtnet); no direct provincial caster. Price shown is HxGN SmartNet Atlantic plan — Can-Net and Brandtnet pricing not public.

markers.name: SCRTN
markers.note: 43 stations in SC plus shared receivers in GA and NC. No professional-licence requirement.

markers.name: NCRTN
markers.note: Perpetual credentials (not annual). Second login included; additional logins $250 each. Free RINEX download.

markers.name: KeyNetGPS
markers.note: Commercial Trimble VRS3Net covering the whole Northeast. A practical paid option in NH, NJ, PA, DE, MD, DC, RI, where no free state caster exists (SmartNet and Trimble VRS Now also cover parts of this region). Pricing not posted; quoted via Keypre or resellers.

markers.name: AlphaRTK
markers.region: US Mid-Atlantic (DE, MD, NJ, PA, DC)
markers.note: No annual plan — the 24-month rolling subscription is the cheapest sustained option ($1,595 / 24 mo). 1-week free trial useful for spot jobs.

markers.name: eGPS Solutions RTN
markers.note: Only RTK network identified with Georgia coverage; GDOT runs no public caster. Plan C "Flex" ($50/day capped $400/mo) is the most practical for occasional use; dual-network Plan A is $2,475/yr.

markers.name: TURN GPS
markers.note: Covers Utah plus Nevada GPS Network (Reno area / northern NV only; Las Vegas not covered).

markers.name: MTSRN
markers.note: 50+ stations; launched March 2022. Free RINEX available; static post-processing does not require subscription.

markers.name: WSRN
markers.note: Transitioning to NATRF2022 datum (port 2022); NAD83(2011) on port 2011. Partner agencies (govt, NGS cooperators) receive free access.

markers.name: C4Gnet
markers.note: Louisiana statewide RTN operated by LSU Center for GeoInformatics. GPS+GLONASS+Galileo+BeiDou. Unlimited RTK tier $3,500/yr. Free post-processing RINEX subscription available separately.

markers.name: CRTN (SOPAC)
markers.note: ~250 reference stations via Scripps (UCSD); aggregates SCIGN, BARD, USGS Pasadena, Caltrans CVSRN, OCRTN, and EarthScope. Universities and schools are exempt from the fee. Significant station overlap with EarthScope (already on this map). Credentials take a week or more to issue.

markers.name: IDOT CORS
markers.note: Under construction — ~70 stations planned; announced November 2024 with federal + state funding. No live NTRIP caster as of May 2026. Interim paid option: ReIL-NET (Kara Company, Chicagoland + Central IL).

markers.name: TxDOT CORS
markers.note: TxDOT employees and contractors only. No hobbyist registration path.

markers.name: CalRTNS
markers.note: Vetted state/county agency partners only. No public registration path.

markers.name: APN
markers.note: Government service (Survey of Israel), licensed surveyors only. WARNING: pervasive military GNSS spoofing across Israel and the surrounding region since Oct 2023 — RTK is unreliable regardless of NTRIP access.

markers.name: IGRS
markers.note: Iraq Geodetic Reference System has only 7 reference stations at 500–800 km spacing — far too sparse for RTK. No public NTRIP caster.

markers.name: Pak-Rehber
markers.note: Operated by SUPARCO Business Solutions. Explicitly restricted to authorised users; no public registration path.

markers.name: SLCORSnet
markers.note: Government network by the Survey Department; coverage mainly Western Province with island-wide rollout ongoing. Bank transfer payment only — may be a barrier for non-residents.

markers.name: CORSnet
markers.note: Private island-wide network, founded 2014. Self-service registration open to individuals; rates issued on inquiry — no public LKR rate card. Mountpoints delivered after payment.

markers.name: SOB VRS
markers.note: 6-station national VRS (Dhaka, Chittagong, Rajshahi, Khulna, Maulavibazar, Rangpur). Pricing unpublished; payment via Rocket/bKash/SureCash requires a Bangladeshi mobile-banking account. Free volunteer Centipede coverage near Chittagong.

markers.name: DrukNet / MiraNet
markers.note: 13 CORS stations across Bhutan. Educational and research accounts are free with an official supporting letter from your institution.

markers.name: НЦГПИ / KazGeoDesy
markers.note: National network operated by KGS. Pricing not publicly listed since rtk.qgeo.kz reverted to a near-empty header; sales-contact only. Kazakh ИИН/БИН and KZT bank transfer needed — foreign self-registration not possible. Baselines ~180 km outside the Astana–Almaty corridor.

markers.name: UZPOS
markers.note: State UZPOS CORS (~30–50 stations) is closed to the public. No rtk2go, Centipede or EarthScope stations within 800 km of Tashkent either. Hobbyists must deploy a private base.

markers.name: ALBCORS
markers.note: State CORS operated by ASIG (national geodetic authority). Application required; no self-service registration and no public NTRIP host. A commercial alternative, SATNET LIVE (landcoal.com), offers trial access.

markers.name: AzPOS
markers.note: Leica Spider VRS backend. Requires a bilateral service agreement with a government office in Baku; no self-service registration and no published tariff. One rtk2go volunteer base covers greater Baku.

markers.name: ARMPOS
markers.note: 12-station network installed 2013, operated by the Cadastre Committee. No public NTRIP host — access restricted to licensed surveyors. No free RTK anywhere in the South Caucasus.

markers.name: GEO-CORS
markers.note: 26-station national CORS network (NAPR). Registration open via Leica Spider Business Center; pricing not publicly listed — contact via geocors.napr.gov.ge. No explicit restriction on non-professional users documented.

markers.name: DVRS
markers.note: 18+ four-constellation stations under Dubai Municipality. Professional application required; no hobbyist registration path. NTRIP endpoint may have migrated — the GeoDubai portal remains the application front-end.

markers.name: SLRB PRN
markers.note: Apply by email with the form from the SLRB page; credentials issued within 1–2 working days. Host:port disclosed in the credentials email only. SLRB notes the service may become paid.

markers.name: AL-CORS-Net / SAAP
markers.note: 189-station VRS Network-RTK on Geo++ GNSMART. Operated under the Ministry of National Defence; no public registration portal or tariff.

markers.name: REGPMOC
markers.note: Single-base stations under IGN/Ministry of Defence (35+ active). Access requires application + payment to IGN; no online self-service portal. IGN's policy does not explicitly exclude individuals, but there is no hobbyist-accessible sign-up path.

markers.name: EFT-CORS
markers.note: Hundreds of stations across Russia, multi-constellation. Day-pass and shorter plans available. Basic 30s RINEX free. 3-day RTK trial available.

markers.name: RTKNet
markers.note: Covers all federal districts; ports 6030–6041 by district. 3-day trial available.

markers.name: HIVE
markers.note: Aggregator of independently owned stations across Russian regions; the station count visible on the landing page contracted sharply between two recent checks (reason unexplained on the site). Pay-per-use: daily RTK per station (prices vary; login required) or hourly post-processing. First ~5 min per station free.

markers.name: ГЕОСПАЙДЕР
markers.note: 200+ stations across NW and Central Russia. Short day/week tiers available. Network RTK in local MSK coordinate system.

markers.name: 千寻知寸 Qianxun
markers.note: 2,700+ stations across 33 provinces, multi-constellation. Chinese nationals can register without a surveying licence. Foreign visitors require a Chinese phone number and national-ID verification — no practical self-service path.

markers.name: 中国移动CORS
markers.note: 4,400+ stations nationwide via China Mobile — the largest of the three commercial options. Chinese nationals can register individually. Foreign visitors require a Chinese phone number and real-name ID verification.

markers.name: Tencent RTK
markers.note: ~2,800+ virtual stations across 33 provinces. Access via enterprise business inquiry only — no self-service pricing. Chinese phone number and likely a Chinese business licence required for commercial use.

markers.name: Re.M.FVG (Marussi)
markers.region: Friuli-Venezia Giulia (Italy) + Slovenian SIGNAL border relays

markers.name: CATNET
markers.note: Free ICGC regional RTK caster for Catalonia. Separate operator and registration from national ERGNSS. Single ICGC account required; no professional licence.

markers.name: GRAFCAN REPCAN
markers.note: 20-station Canary Islands network. Pricing not published — see tiendavirtual.grafcan.es. Free IGN ERGNSS (ergnss-tr.ign.es:2101) covers the Canaries at no cost and is the recommended first option.

markers.name: InaCORS
markers.note: Sparse map pins — the caster exposes 4 network-solution mounts, not individual station pins. Coverage is denser on Java and Bali; outer islands (Papua, Kalimantan) have gaps.

markers.name: IGAC MAGNA-ECO
markers.note: 137 physical stations broadcast on port 2102; VRS / network-RTK on port 2101.

markers.name: SPSLux
markers.note: 13 stations, free. iMAX and VRS correction types; free registration at ACT portal (zero-cost subscription).

markers.name: IceCORS
markers.note: 33 stations, free. Nearest-station selector and VRS3 network-RTK available.

markers.name: CORS-KOREA
markers.note: Federated single-base feed from 8 Korean agencies. Email-only registration; no Korean ID required. NTRIP password is the literal string 'gnss', not the portal login password. Accounts auto-delete after 50 days inactivity. Separate NGII VRS/FKP network-solution service requires Korean mobile-identity verification.

markers.name: MBC RTK / B-RTK
markers.note: Nationwide commercial broadcast+NTRIP RTK network operated by MBC (terrestrial broadcaster). Access is bundled with custom B-RTK receiver hardware sold to fleet and OEM integrators; no self-serve consumer NTRIP signup at any price. Free hobbyist alternative: CORS-KOREA via the GNSS Data Center.

markers.name: APOS
markers.note: Short-term use: €20/day (RTK, centimetre accuracy) or €2/day (DGPS, decimetre accuracy). Monthly subscription also available. €50 one-time setup fee. Free for Austrian agricultural users with farm registration.

markers.name: MIRAI / Go!GNSS
markers.note: 16 Japan-located physical stations (caster also re-streams ~309 worldwide partner stations from AU/NZ/US/CA/etc.). Free registration plus a separate NtripCaster authorization step; accounts auto-expire after 365 days inactivity.

markers.name: sapos RP
markers.note: The only SAPOS state that charges for standard RTK — all other SAPOS states offer it free. One-time €100 setup fee applies (amortised in the figure shown). Agriculture has a cheaper €150/device/yr R-HEPS tier; no free hobbyist path.

markers.name: ACORN
markers.note: Extends with 1 station in RI, 2 in southern MA, 1 on Long Island NY — useful fallback for Rhode Island.

markers.name: AzCORS
markers.note: 52-station Arizona CORS (37 ADWR + 15 EarthScope/NPS). Free registration via ADWR; Leica SBC platform. Actual NTRIP port confirmed post-registration.

markers.name: GCGC RTN
markers.note: 52-station RTK network (Univ. of Southern Mississippi Gulf Coast Geospatial Center). Free; no professional licence required. Trimble Pivot platform; VRS availability unconfirmed.

markers.name: KOPOS
markers.note: Operational since 2012. One-time €20 registration fee also applies; monthly (€60) and 6-month (€250) plans available. NTRIP credentials issued inside the online portal after account creation.

markers.name: OTC GNSS
markers.note: Saharan south not covered. Shorter durations from 60 TND/day also available.

markers.name: AGRS.NL / AGRS.BES
markers.note: ~30 stations across the Netherlands + 7 streams on the BES Islands (Bonaire, Saba, Sint Eustatius), free, anonymous. ntrip.kadaster.nl:2101 or :443 (TLS). Single-base, not VRS. TU Delft mirror at gnss1.tudelft.nl:2101 carries a Netherlands subset.

markers.name: FINPOS
markers.note: Government RTK service, but access is granted only for research with written justification (renewable every 3 months). FINPOS DGNSS is advertised separately for general use but is out of scope for cm-grade work.

markers.name: Rete GPS Emilia-Romagna
markers.note: The region's previously free public RTK network was discontinued; the same physical stations now carry commercial corrections only (NetGEO/TopNET Live).

markers.name: OS Net
markers.note: Ordnance Survey runs ~110 reference stations but distributes corrections only through licensed commercial resellers (Leica HxGN SmartNet, Trimble VRS Now, Topcon TopNet Live, AXIO-NET, others). No direct OS endpoint and no free hobbyist tier.

markers.name: Tailte Éireann GNSS Network
markers.note: Free RINEX post-processing only (gnss.tailte.ie); real-time corrections sold through commercial resellers only (Trimble VRS Now ~€980–1,390/yr, HxGN SmartNet). ~18 free volunteer bases on rtk2go + Centipede.

markers.name: BIGF Gibraltar
markers.note: Tide-gauge GNSS station, RINEX archive only — no real-time RTK service in Gibraltar.

markers.name: ERGAND / PCAR (Andorra)
markers.note: No Andorran national caster. EPN station PCAR00AND0 (Pic de Carroi, ~5 km from Andorra la Vella) streams free single-base RTCM via EUREF-IP broadcasters — a BKG, ROB, or ASI account gives access. Spanish ERGNSS (ergnss-ip.ign.es) is the practical VRS option.

markers.name: San Marino RSMC
markers.note: One reference station (RSMC) distributing raw GNSS data for post-processing. No real-time RTK service.

markers.name: Survey Department Brunei
markers.note: Internal-use cadastral CORS only; no public NTRIP service has been announced.

markers.name: Kadaster Sint Maarten CORS
markers.note: Pricing targets professional surveyors. Nearest free fallback is EarthScope CN59 on Anguilla (~20 km, NULA non-commercial).

markers.name: RGNA / INEGI
markers.note: INEGI publishes free 15-second RINEX from ~30 national stations for post-processing (SFTP, anonymous). No real-time NTRIP/RTK streaming. Commercial NTRIP RTK is sold by several private resellers (Red CORS México, Survey+, TopNET Live).

markers.name: Red CORS México
markers.note: Largest commercial NTRIP network in Mexico (60–85+ cities), resold under several vendor brands. Sold per month or per year in MXN; Mexican phone/banking needed at sign-up. Survey+ MX and TopNET Live México are parallel commercial options.

markers.name: IGN Guatemala Red CORS
markers.note: Guatemala's national mapping institute publishes free RINEX files from 16 reference stations for post-processing. No real-time NTRIP service is offered.

markers.name: IP CORS Honduras
markers.note: Five government reference stations (Tegucigalpa, San Pedro Sula, Juticalpa, Siguatepeque, La Ceiba) publish free RINEX files for post-processing. No real-time NTRIP service is offered.

markers.name: INETER CORS
markers.note: INETER publishes free RINEX files for post-processing via the Catastro Físico portal; no domestic NTRIP service. For real-time, EarthScope NOTA hosts two free non-commercial Nicaraguan streams (Chinandega/CNG2 and central/JAPO) under a NULA.

markers.name: CNR/IGCN CORS
markers.note: CNR/IGCN hosts the SSIA reference station near San Salvador and publishes free RINEX for post-processing via the eCNR portal. No real-time NTRIP service is offered.

markers.name: Survey3G NTRIP
markers.note: Only commercial RTK provider identified in the country; ~90% national coverage. Free alternative: EarthScope NOTA station SSIA near San Salvador (NULA, non-commercial).

markers.name: SIRGAS-CHILE / IGM
markers.note: Chile's military geographic institute publishes free RINEX files from 180+ reference stations. A real-time NTRIP service was announced in 2025 but the public endpoint is not yet working.

markers.name: KollNET
markers.note: Only confirmed paid hobbyist-accessible NTRIP service in Chile; 8 stations from Santiago to Frutillar. Will become less relevant once the planned public IGM/SHOA national network goes live.

markers.name: PNG2020 reference stations
markers.note: Sparse network of ~6 scientific reference stations underpinning the PNG2020 datum; baselines are too long for reliable RTK outside Lae and Port Moresby. A subscription NTRIP service (ASPNG-hosted) has been discussed but is not yet active.

markers.name: Fiji CORS
markers.note: Ten CORS sites were installed in 2022 covering Viti Levu, Vanua Levu and the outer islands. The access policy is still under development; no public NTRIP caster has been announced.

markers.name: SENCORS
markers.note: PROCASEF + JICA stations delivering VRS / i-MAX corrections; restored March 2026 after a disk failure. Subscription required; tariff not published.

markers.name: CNIGS
markers.note: No public NTRIP service. A 23-station national CORS plan (2015) and a 2018 expansion announcement never produced a live caster. Use PPP corrections or a local base.

markers.name: MI-GLIS CORS
markers.note: National CORS network operated by the land registry; paid since July 2024 but tariffs are quote-only and the workflow targets institutions. No public host:port and no published hobbyist tier.

markers.name: Hoda Pro
markers.note: Paid RTK service from Iran's National Cartographic Center, run on the IPGN station network. The subscription portal is blocked outside Iran and rates are not published; sign-up needs an Iranian national ID and Iranian banking.

markers.name: SHAMIM
markers.note: Cadastre-programme network installed 2016-17: registration requires an Iranian national ID, an Iranian mobile number, and a specific GNSS receiver serial registered against the account. No documented sign-up path for hobbyists; endpoints firewalled outside Iran.

markers.name: REPANGOL
markers.note: Eighteen IGCA CORS installed 2010 underpin the national reference frame, but no public NTRIP endpoint has ever been published and the repangol.net portal is offline.

markers.name: Madagascar — no national RTK
markers.note: FTM, the national mapping agency, maintains only passive geodetic control — no NTRIP service. Two volunteer Centipede bases (near Mahajanga and Antananarivo) cover ~35 km each; the south coast, far north and east have no free RTK.

markers.name: Bahamas Lands & Surveys CORS
markers.note: 23-station Trimble CORS deployed ~2020 by Spatial Dimension for the Department of Lands and Surveys; access is institutional, no public NTRIP endpoint.

markers.name: RECI
markers.note: Five-station BNETD-CIGN CORS upgraded to RTK NTRIP mode in 2022, but the public host:port has not been published — access via institutional channel only.

markers.name: Ghana National CORS Network
markers.note: ~60 stations unveiled Aug 2025 by Lands Commission/SMD; target 100 by end of 2025. No public NTRIP endpoint published; access via licensed-surveyor channel.

markers.name: IGNTOGO National CORS
markers.note: National CORS network made mandatory for all topographic and cadastral work by a March 2026 inter-ministerial communiqué (three-month compliance window). No public host:port; credentials issued by IGNTOGO on request. The igntogo.tg portal was unreachable as of May 2026.

markers.name: IGN Bénin CORS
markers.note: 7-station MCA-funded GNSS CORS network. Host:port not public; disclosed via IGN Bénin / CatIS registration (service-public.bj PS01085). Hobbyist eligibility unconfirmed — service oriented toward cadastral use.

markers.name: ССТП РБ / Belgeodesiya
markers.note: Residency-only service; signed paper contract with Belgeodesiya required. Western GNSS hardware import is suspended under EU/UK/US sanctions since 2022.

markers.name: MOLDPOS
markers.note: National VRS network; no surveying licence required. Free test mounts (FZUTM, FZUASM, etc.) available with credentials moldpos/moldpos — trial without subscribing.

markers.name: MAKPOS
markers.note: 14 stations; Galileo-capable since 2020. Subscription via Spider Business Center; rates are not published — one community source mentions free 3G access, unconfirmed.

markers.name: Réseau GNSS ANCFCC
markers.note: 60 stations. Real-time RTK and network-RTK confirmed. Licensed cadastral professionals only; no individual sign-up path.

markers.name: itri GNSS Network
markers.note: 231 stations; Morocco's first private GNSS network (launched 2020). Marketed to surveying professionals; rates are not published.

markers.name: MoSRef
markers.note: Free registration; GPS+GLONASS+BeiDou (since 2021). Single-base RTK and VRS; four HK partner stations extend coverage across the Pearl River Delta.

markers.name: OmanCORSnet
markers.note: Operated by NSGIA. The caster at omancorsnet.gov.om:2101 advertises VRS/MAX/Nearest network-RTK mountpoints, but streaming credentials are issued only via the Spider Business Center after manual approval; no hobbyist tier confirmed.

markers.name: QCORS
markers.note: Operated by CGIS; serves licensed surveyors and government users. No public self-registration.

markers.name: GNET
markers.note: ~60 continuous GNSS stations spanning Greenland for ice-sheet and geodetic research (KDS / DTU Space / Asiaq). RINEX freely downloadable from Dataforsyningen for post-processing; no real-time NTRIP service.

markers.name: Rwanda Geodetic Network
markers.note: RLMUA operates ~10 CORS sites with free post-processed RINEX; no real-time NTRIP endpoint published. Three EarthScope stations near Lake Kivu (Rubavu/Kibuye) stream free real-time corrections — useful for western Rwanda.

markers.name: NYAWIPEV (Centipede) + IGS Ny-Ålesund
markers.note: Single free Centipede base (NYAWIPEV) at the AWIPEV Arctic research station covers ~20–40 km around Ny-Ålesund. Norway's CPOS does not extend to Svalbard. Longyearbyen has no public RTK — deploy a local base or use PPP.

markers.name: Botswana DSM CORS
markers.note: Department of Surveys and Mapping has built ~55 CORS at 30–40 km spacing since 2011, covering most of the country. No public NTRIP host:port; access requires direct DSM engagement.

markers.name: CENACARTA CORS
markers.note: 8 CENACARTA reference stations exist (Maputo, Beira, Chimoio, Tete, Quelimane, Nacala, Lichinga, Xai-Xai) but no public NTRIP endpoint is published; built for post-processing.

markers.name: ZINGSA CORS
markers.note: National reference station network run by ZINGSA. Statutory fee of US$200/yr (S.I. 47 of 2023), but no published caster address or self-service signup — credentials come only after a direct enquiry to ZINGSA.

markers.name: NIGNET
markers.note: OSGOF's ~15-station geodetic network is fronted by the MIRAnet portal at miranet.nignet.net (caster ntrip.nignet.net:21011). Accounts are manually approved and described as fee-paying, with no published tariff or hobbyist tier. 500-1,000 km inter-station baselines exceed the ~50 km RTK envelope until the announced 165-station expansion lands.

markers.name: TTAGN
markers.note: Five-station national network (Surveys and Mapping Division). Ministry lists the service but the gpscors.gov.tt portal stopped resolving externally — access likely ministry-network-internal or limited to licensed surveyors.

markers.name: Umhvørvisstovan GNSS
markers.note: Four reference stations (Klaksvík, Vestmanna, Trongisvágur, Argir) advertised for surveying and construction firms. No caster, port, or tariff published — access entirely via direct contact. Danish GPSnet.dk does not cover the Faroes.

markers.name: ESA CORS
markers.note: ~40 stations operated by the Egyptian Survey Authority for cadastral and infrastructure projects, concentrated in Cairo and the Nile Delta. No public NTRIP caster or self-service registration.

markers.name: Acnovo NTRIP
markers.note: Private commercial NTRIP provider — the only one identified in Venezuela. Billing cycle (monthly vs per-session) and station count not stated publicly; credentials issued only after payment.

markers.name: Yemen GAS
markers.note: Civil conflict since 2015 has halted public geodetic services. The General Survey Authority website is unreachable; no public NTRIP caster, RINEX archive, or volunteer base anywhere in Yemen.

markers.name: CYPOS
markers.note: 7 stations on the south coast and plateau; operational since 2010. Profile must be validated in person at a Citizen Service Centre — a practical barrier for visitors without a Cypriot civil registration number. A free EUREF-IP single-base station (NICO, Nicosia) covers ~30 km radius via BKG/ROB/ASI broadcasters.

markers.name: GEOCUBA GNSS
markers.note: 13 permanent GNSS stations operational since 2019 under GEOCUBA (MINFAR). NTRIP service confirmed in a 2024 paper but no public host, port, or registration portal has been published. US OFAC regulations add a further practical barrier for visitors.

markers.name: GPSnet.dk
markers.note: Denmark's main cadastral VRS network. Short-term (weekly / monthly) and annual plans available; price shown after login. Volunteer fallback: ~17 rtk2go bases and ~18 Centipede nodes, mostly in Jutland.

markers.name: RTKconnect
markers.note: 111-station FKP/VRS network; 10 km average baseline. Approved by Klimadatastyrelsen.

markers.name: NGD / IGN FI CORS (Laos)
markers.note: No public NTRIP service. The IGN FI portfolio page (updated May 2024) describes a Lao CORS installation; no host:port, mountpoint, or access path is disclosed. First pilot CORS commissioned 2013 (ComNav, BeiDou). Deploy a local base or use Galileo HAS.

markers.name: Lesotho (TrigNet ZA fallback)
markers.note: No local caster. Nearest free service is South Africa's TrigNet at trignet.co.za:2101, but the closest station (Bloemfontein) sits ~210 km from Maseru — too far for cm-grade single-base RTK. Deploy a local base or use Galileo HAS.

markers.name: Liechtenstein (swipos / APOS coverage)
markers.note: No Liechtenstein caster. Swiss swipos (paid, ~CHF 1,500/yr or CHF 0.50/min pay-per-use) covers the country directly; Austrian APOS adds coverage and is free for farmers via eAMA. Centipede and rtk2go have volunteer bases within 20–60 km.
